units.q1: Why shouldn't a severely hypothermic, confused person be rewarmed quickly in the field?
units.a1:
Hypothermia (very cold, shivering, confused or drowsy): get them indoors or to a sheltered place as quickly as possible, out of the wind and off the cold ground. Remove wet clothing and wrap them in dry blankets, a sleeping bag or towels, with the head covered. Handle them gently. If they're fully awake, give a warm non-alcoholic drink and something sugary like chocolate; give no drinks to someone who isn't fully awake. You can also warm them skin to skin under dry blankets. Don't use a hot bath, hot-water bottle, heat lamp or fire, don't rub their arms, legs, hands or feet, and don't give alcohol. If they stop breathing normally, start CPR and keep warming them. Call emergency services for anyone you think has hypothermia; don't drive them yourself if an ambulance can come.

Source: NHS, Hypothermia; St John Ambulance (UK), Hypothermia; CDC, Preventing Hypothermia. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

units.q1: What does the name Jebba mean?
units.a1: The name Jebba means "water is flowing here [1]." It is associated with relics and monuments in Jebba town, which is on the Niger River. [1]
units.q2: and what does its name mean?
units.a2: Jebba means "water is flowing here" and is associated with relics and monuments that highlight past interactions with Europeans and Colonial masters [2].
units.gold: The word Jebba means "water is flowing here".

units.q1: How many inhabitants does Corralejo have and how many guest beds?
units.a1: Corralejo has about 18,000 inhabitants and provides over 20,000 guest beds [1].
units.q2: and how many guest beds does it have?
units.a2: Corralejo has about 18,000 inhabitants and provides over 20,000 guest beds [3].
units.gold: Corralejo has about 18,000 inhabitants, with 20,000 guest beds available.

units.q1: When is the rainy season at Lagunas de Chacahua National Park?
units.a1: The rainy season at Lagunas de Chacahua National Park is from June to October-November [1].
units.q2: and when is the rainy season there?
units.a2: The rainy season at Lagunas de Chacahua National Park is from June to October-November [5]. The season brings frequent rain, which can affect visibility and travel.
units.gold: Mostly hot through the year, with maximum temperatures reached around late spring. Rainy season is from June to October-November.
